additive_change_to_existing_type.previous_derives: Debug + Clone + Copy + PartialEq + Eq + serde::Deserialize + JsonSchema
additive_change_to_existing_type.disclosure: Additive wire-shape change. The new Serialize impl produces "invariant"|"existence"|"call_path" strings — matches JsonSchema's snake_case wire shape exactly. No inbound JSON breakage. Roundtrip verified via counterexample_bundle_summary_dto_roundtrip_snake_case test.

architectural_decisions.stub_first_to_avoid_signature_churn: Both `get` and `list` return machine-readable stub errors in m8-01 instead of returning Unimplemented. m8-03 can wire redb read logic without changing the public signature that the future MCP wrappers will bind to. This is the 'single-call dispatch, no follow-up cycle' pattern from m7-07's SessionStopPersistence.
architectural_decisions.context_borrows_hypothesis_ctx: CounterexampleContext<'a> borrows HypothesisTestContext<'a> rather than holding &QueryEngine directly. Mirrors m7-05 SessionLifecycleContext borrowing ProbeContext — avoids dual ownership and inherits the engines map lifetime.
architectural_decisions.internal_enum_at_module_scope: CounterexampleShrinkInput + CounterexampleOutput + CounterexampleBundle stay at module scope (counterexample.rs), NOT in output.rs. They carry proptest runtime config / Vec<TraceEvent> which we don't want on the wire yet. m8-03 promotes the wire-shape sub-types to output.rs as *Dto types.
architectural_decisions.wire_dtos_are_summary_only: Wire DTOs omit events vector intentionally. Bundles are returned by handle (bundle_id) and re-fetched, never streamed in tool responses. Rationale (B3 in scoping doc): avoids forcing JsonSchema through Vec<TraceEvent>.
architectural_decisions.proptest_is_dev_dependency_only: promote to runtime dep is m8-02's decision. Wires at workspace level so future cycles can move it without a Cargo.toml change.
architectural_decisions.no_chronos_cli_workspace_member_in_m8_01: Adding a new crate to host nothing violates minimalism. m8-04 brings the CLI wrapper, when the dispatcher has at least 2 entry points that the CLI shell-glue can hit.

followups.scope: Promote proptest to runtime [dependencies] in chronos-services. Implement `ChronosCounterexampleService::shrink`: convert HypothesisInput → proptest::Strategy (this is the experimental risk of M8), run proptest::TestRunner for up to `max_rounds` rounds (default 64), observe HypothesisVerdict via the existing hypothesis_test dispatcher, and emit CounterexampleBundle on first run that finds the violation + a minimised counterexample after the shrink passes. Add 4-6 unit tests using a known-failing hypothesis (e.g., invariant: event_count < 5 on a busyloop fixture). A-min scope.

Provision `counterexample_bundles` redb table (key: bundle_id, value: serialised Bundle envelope). Replace `get`/`list` stub bodies with redb-backed lookups. Add `CounterexampleBundleDto` (wire shape WITH Vec<TraceEvent>) gated behind an `include_events: bool` param to keep roundtrip small. Add 3 v2 MCP wrappers `counterexample_shrink` / `counterexample_get` / `counterexample_list` in chronos-mcp/src/server.rs. Sandbox smoke against test_exit_immediate + test_busyloop fixtures (no test_echo — doesn't exist). A-lite scope.

Add crates/chronos-cli workspace member. Thin driver: parses `chronos test <bundle_id>` and `chronos replay <bundle_id>` subcommands, calls `counterexample_get` / session_load via the same RPC surface the MCP server uses. No reimplementation of dispatcher algorithms. A-min scope.

M8 close: run an acceptance scenario that picks a known failing hypothesis on a test_busyloop fixture, ships it through counterexample_shrink → counterexample_get, and verifies the persisted bundle preserves the violation property after shrink. Final M8 report. A-lite scope.

naming_collision_disclosure.trigger: m7-06 close report §7 labelled a wishlist (live-probe perf, MCP hardening, distributed tracing) as 'M8'. The actual roadmap M8 (ROADMAP.md line 179) is counterexample shrinking + test intelligence.
naming_collision_disclosure.resolution: Adopted the roadmap M8 (this cycle). The wishlist items remain valid but are post-M8 backlog: m7-09 (attach), m9.5 (otel export), m10.5 (multi-process fanout), m11.5 (MCP observability). See `docs/milestones/m8-counterexample-shrinking-scoping.md` § "Naming-collision honest disclosure" for the full item-by-item mapping.
